title: Introduce surge-horizon allocator and deferred headroom penalty for fair burst leasing
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Adds a new surge leasing allocator that prioritizes sustained utilization while preventing short-lived burst starvation; includes telemetry for deferred headroom events and a configurable penalty window.
description:
Context and motivation: Dedicated fleets can see short microbursts that starve tenants who have been using headroom consistently; current soft-bursting allows immediate leasing which can cause oscillation and unfairness during capacity pressure. This PR introduces the 'surge-horizon allocator' plus a 'deferred headroom penalty' mechanism to smooth burst grants and favor tenants with sustained utilization.

Summary of changes: Implemented a new allocator component (SurgeHorizonAllocator) that considers three signals: 1) recent sustained utilization (30m EWMA), 2) burst request pattern (microburst score), and 3) cluster-level slack horizon (predictive free capacity for next N minutes). When capacity is contended, the allocator applies a deferred penalty window to tenants that have recently consumed large instantaneous bursts, reducing their immediate surge priority for a configurable duration. The mechanism is tunable via dedicated capacity config and integrates with existing reservation ledgers and burst token pool.

Files changed (high level): runtime/surge_horizon/allocator.go - core algorithm and scoring; runtime/surge_horizon/strategy_test.go - unit tests and deterministic scenarios; controllers/fleet_controller.go - wiring allocator into admission path; telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml - new metrics and labels; observability/alerts.yml - new alert for high deferred-penalty pressure; api/dedicated_schema.proto - new config fields for penalty_window and horizon_lookahead; docs/ops/allocator-runbook.md - operational notes and tuning guide; examples/dedicated/penalty-config.yaml - example config for production.

Commits (summary): commit 1: scaffold surge_horizon package and interfaces; commit 2: implement core scoring and deferred penalty state machine; commit 3: integrate with reservation ledger and burst token pool adapter; commit 4: add telemetry counters and histogram labels for deferred_penalty_age and surge_horizon_score; commit 5: unit + e2e style tests and deterministic harness; commit 6: docs, runbook, and rollout plan.

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover fairness invariants and scoring monotonicity. Added deterministic harness tests that simulate 1-min microbursts versus sustained tenants over 2-hour windows. CI initially surfaced a flake in the deterministic harness (race between token refill goroutine and test harness), fixed by introducing a test-only sync hook. Full integration suite passed on re-run (build/test/lint all green).

Observability and telemetry: New metrics: redwood.surge_horizon.score (gauge), redwood.surge_horizon.deferred_penalty_count (counter), redwood.surge_horizon.deferred_penalty_age (histogram), and a tag redwood.tenant.burst_policy to distinguish legacy vs deferred policies. Dashboards added show tenant-level penalty churn and aggregate fairness delta vs baseline. Alerts added for sustained penalty_count > threshold for > 10m to prevent emergent starvation.

Review conversation (high level): Jordan Lee: "Algorithm looks sound; need clarity on tuning knobs and safety defaults. Can we make penalty_window conservative by default?" Author (Anika): "Yes — default is 10m. Documented in runbook with examples and a conservative toggle to disable deferred penalties per fleet." Priya Menon: "Edge case: what if a large tenant legitimately needs multiple bursts (e.g., nightly batch)? Would penalty cause SLA misses?" Author: "We added opt-out labels per-tenant and admission policy that can treat scheduled batch windows as exempt; also added a decay function to let penalties evaporate faster if sustained utilization resumes." Evan Chen: "Ensure integration with Dedicated autoscaler so we don't oscillate scale-up/down; add a dry-run flag for the allocator." Author: "Added autoscaler integration with a 'surge_horizon_dry_run' flag and a rollout plan to start in dry-run for 48h. Confirmed no autoscaler toggles during dry-run in tests."

Migration and rollout plan: 1) Canary rollout to a single low-risk region (eu-west-1) with surge_horizon_dry_run=true for 48h; 2) Enable scoring telemetry and compare fairness delta baseline; 3) After verification, enable dry_run=false and penalty_window=10m in 10% of fleets; 4) Observe metrics for 72h, increment to 50% then 100% as long as no starvation alerts. Documentation updated with tuning recommendations for penalty_window, horizon_lookahead, and example size-based exemptions.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default configuration keeps legacy behavior if penalty_window=0. All new config fields are additive. The allocator has a safety tradeoff: under extreme overcommit it steps down to a permissive mode which allows bursts to proceed (fail-open) to avoid hard denials. The perf impact is minimal in median P95 token-path latency (0.6% regression at extreme load in synthetic tests) and the tradeoff has been documented.

Operational notes: ops runbook includes steps to identify tenants with frequent deferred penalties, how to add tenant exemptions, and how to tune the horizon_lookahead for predictable load profiles. Also includes sample queries.

Merge outcome: PR was merged via squash merge after approvals from Jordan and Priya and CI green. Change goes out as opt-in (dry-run) and then staged enabling per rollout plan.

Related work: builds on reservation-ledger refactor (ENG-2176) and token-pool instrumentation (ENG-2241).
commit_summary: scaffold surge_horizon package; implement scoring and deferred penalty state machine; integrate with reservation ledger & token pool adapter; add telemetry & histograms; add deterministic harness tests and fix race; docs and runbook
notes_for_reviewers: Key reviewers: verify fairness invariants in strategy_test.go and validate that the safety fail-open path is adequate. Pay attention to the default penalty_window and horizon_lookahead values and whether they are conservative enough for enterprise fleets.
